name: Consumer Credit Directive II
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: applies from November 2026; evaluation of the 2008 Directive
summary: The new Directive applies from 20 November 2026. The evaluation of the 2008 Directive it replaces found that consumer protection and a single credit market had been only partially achieved, and that digital lending raised new risks. The impact assessment forecast a reduction in consumer detriment of around EUR 2 billion in 2021-2030.

literature.citation: European Commission (2020), Evaluation of Directive 2008/48/EC on credit agreements for consumers, SWD(2020) 254 (with report COM(2020) 963)
literature.title: Evaluation of Directive 2008/48/EC on credit agreements for consumers
literature.headline: Objectives only partially achieved; withdrawal and early repayment rights and standard information reduced detriment; digitalisation and new products created risks the Directive did not cover
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the 2008 rules had raised consumer protection but had not created a single credit market and were outdated for online lending.

literature.citation: European Commission (2021), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on consumer credits (executive summary), SWD(2021) 171 (full IA SWD(2021) 170)
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Directive on consumer credits (executive summary)
literature.headline: Up to 46 million people affected by problems with the old rules; preferred option to cut consumer detriment by about EUR 2 billion in 2021-2030
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the new rules to save consumers about EUR 2 billion over ten years.
